title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
slides: Can Flox Intelligence stop wildlife killing trains?
Rail strikes kill thousands of animals yearly worldwide.
The AI predicts animal movement before it happens.
Airports and roads can deploy the same system now.
Ask your local transit agency if they use it.
thread_text:
1. AI vs. Wildlife

Thousands of animals are struck by trains every year, but a new AI called Flox Intelligence might predict their movements before they step onto the tracks.

2. Why It Matters

Rail strikes are a leading cause of wildlife mortality worldwide, often going unnoticed by the public and transit agencies alike.

3. How It Works

Flox Intelligence uses machine learning to forecast animal paths in real time, giving trains a chance to slow down or stop in advance.

4. Beyond Railways

Airports and highways face the same problem, and the same predictive system can be deployed there with minimal changes.

5. Your Move

Ask your local transit agency if they're using Flox Intelligence or similar technology. If not, why not?

instagram.caption:
Thousands of animals die on train tracks every year, and most transit agencies don't even track the number.

Flox Intelligence built AI that predicts where wildlife will move before they reach the rails, giving trains time to slow down or stop. 🚆

The same system works at airports and on highways, no major changes needed.

If you make content about transport, environment, or tech, this is a concrete story you can localize: check whether your region's rail or road operator has tested anything like it. 🛤️

Airports near you might already be using something similar without saying so. 🛫
